sector: NZ Diversified REIT (Industrial / Office / Large Format Retail)
overview: Argosy Property is an NZX-listed diversified commercial property investor owning a $2.24 billion portfolio of 49 industrial, office and large-format retail buildings, concentrated in Auckland (72% of value) with the balance in Wellington and select regional centres. The company earns contracted rental income from a diversified tenant base including central government agencies, logistics operators and retailers, and is progressively re-weighting the portfolio toward industrial and green-certified assets. Argosy operates as an internally managed property company (not a unit trust), listed on the NZX Main Board with a 31 March financial year-end.

business_model.summary: Argosy earns recurring rental income from long-term commercial leases across three property sectors, supplemented by capital growth from active asset management, rent reviews, development (build-to-core) and portfolio recycling (selling non-core assets to fund green industrial development). Net property income was $120.8 million in FY2026, up 3.3% on the prior year, with net distributable income of $60.9 million (up 9.1%).
business_model.customer_type: B2B / institutional and government tenants on long-dated commercial leases (WALT 5.0 years); tenant base includes NZ Government departments/agencies (~31% of rental income), logistics and industrial occupiers, and large-format retailers
business_model.geographic_mix: Auckland 72% of portfolio value, Wellington 25%, North Island regional/South Island 3%

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-cap diversified NZX property company (~$1.3-1.5bn market cap range); not sector-dominant in any single category but positioned as a diversified alternative to single-sector specialists (Goodman/PFI in industrial, Precinct in premium Auckland/Wellington office, Kiwi in retail)

moat_factors.description: Spread across industrial, office and large-format retail reduces single-sector cyclicality and vacancy risk versus pure-play peers
~31% of rental income from NZ Government agencies (MBIE, NZ Post, Parliamentary Service) provides income stability and low credit risk

39% of portfolio green-certified (target 50% by FY2031); 6 Green Star developments (224 Neilson Street, Mt Richmond) attract premium tenants and support NABERSNZ ratings, increasingly valued by institutional tenants and financiers
$725m syndicated bank facility across five banks plus green bond programme provides diversified, relatively low-cost funding versus smaller peers
Established NZX-listed operator since 1962 but no structural barrier to entry versus larger, better-capitalised industrial specialists (Goodman) or premium office landlords (Precinct)

weaknesses: No dominant scale in any one sector — sub-scale versus industrial specialist Goodman Property Trust and premium office specialist Precinct
Wellington office exposure carries government tenant concentration and softer market fundamentals than Auckland
Portfolio still under-rented (9.3% below market as at FY2026) which is a double-edged sword — upside on reviews but also indicates historically soft market rents
Occupancy (94.6%) trails best-in-class industrial peers; office segment occupancy (94.2%) reflects leasing softness

growth_drivers: Green industrial development pipeline: completion of 224 Neilson Street (both warehouses, 6 Green Star) and Mt Richmond Stage 1 (Warehouse 6, leased to Viatris) progressively lifting industrial weighting toward the 60-70% target from 55% currently

Portfolio recycling: divestment of non-core assets (4 Henderson Place sold $40m settled April 2026; 143 Lambton Quay sold $6m settled May 2026; further six non-core properties worth $139m identified for medium-term sale) to fund development and reduce debt

Rent reversion: portfolio 9.3% under-rented (ex-development market rent) provides embedded mark-to-market upside on renewal; FY2026 delivered 3.5% annualised rental growth on reviews (4.4% industrial, 2.4% office, 2.6% LFR)
Master-planning of Mt Richmond Road and Neilson Street Auckland industrial estates for further green industrial repositioning
Falling interest rates reducing interest expense ($39.1m FY2026 vs $41.6m prior) as debt refinances at lower weighted average rates (4.65% at FY2026 vs 5.11% FY2025), improving distributable income
Potential earthquake-prone building regime reform (proposed Sept 2025) could materially reduce compliance/remediation costs across the portfolio, particularly benefiting low-seismic Auckland assets
Insurance captive subsidiary delivering premium stabilisation and improved coverage terms amid a softening insurance market

business.description: ~31% of rental income from government tenants and ~25% of portfolio value in Wellington; government agency space consolidation/cutbacks and public sector fiscal restraint are an ongoing leasing risk even though near-term expiries (MBIE, NZ Post) were successfully renewed in FY2026

business.risk: Leasing market softness / extended decision timeframes
business.description: Management noted longer leasing decision-making cycles through FY2026 amid geopolitical and economic uncertainty, though enquiry improved into H2
Meaningful lease expiries clustered in coming years (per lease expiry profile chart) require active re-leasing; occupancy of 94.6% leaves vacancy to backfill
Green industrial pipeline (Mt Richmond further stages, Neilson Street) carries construction cost, timing and lease-up risk typical of build-to-core development

financial.description: Gearing of 37.2% (36.1% post held-for-sale settlements) sits toward the upper-middle of the 30-40% target band; $855.5m of interest-bearing debt with green bonds (ARG020 $100m maturing Oct-2026, ARG030 $125m maturing Oct-2027) requiring refinancing in a still-elevated (though falling) rate environment

NTA and reported profit are heavily influenced by independent valuations (CBRE, Colliers, JLL) and cap-rate movements; FY2026's $58.5m revaluation gain (2.7% on book value) followed $72.7m in FY2025 — a favourable but potentially reversible cycle

Board explicitly noted AFFO volatility (from maintenance capex, leasing incentives, swap close-outs) prompted a switch to an FFO-based payout policy (80-95% of FFO); underlying free cash generation can vary materially year to year

regulatory.description: Proposed Sept-2025 government reform to replace the NBS framework is expected to be a net positive (lower remediation costs, Auckland largely excluded) but final legislative form and timing remain uncertain
Healthy Homes-style and emissions-reduction compliance costs (decarbonisation retrofits, e.g. $13m MBIE project at 15 Stout St) are being progressively funded but add capex intensity

macro.description: RBNZ OCR at 2.25% as of May 2026 with market expectations of gradual increases toward ~3% into 2027; a re-tightening cycle would pressure interest cover and valuations after a benign FY2026

macro.risk: NZ economic cycle / government fiscal restraint
macro.description: Domestic economic conditions described by management as facing 'a range of headwinds'; public sector cost-cutting is a direct read-through to Argosy's government-tenanted Wellington assets
NZX property valuations are sensitive to institutional cap-rate assumptions, which move with long bond yields and risk premia independent of underlying rental income

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ commercial property sector emerging from a multi-year valuation downcycle (2022-2024 cap-rate expansion) into modest recovery, with FY2026 delivering a second consecutive year of revaluation gains (industrial and large-format retail leading); industrial remains the structurally favoured sub-sector on logistics/e-commerce tailwinds, while office faces more mixed fundamentals with a bifurcation between premium/green-certified stock and older assets
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — rental income is contractually defensive (long WALT, fixed/CPI reviews) but capital values and reported profit are cyclical and sensitive to interest rates and cap rates
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — REIT/property company with ~$855m of debt and 37% gearing; falling OCR and swap rates directly reduce interest expense and support cap-rate compression; a renewed rate-hiking cycle (as some banks now forecast into 2027) would be a headwind to both distributable income and NTA
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Minimal direct FX exposure — pure NZD-denominated domestic property portfolio, tenants and debt
key_input_costs: Construction/development costs for green industrial pipeline
Insurance premiums (mitigated by captive insurance subsidiary)
Bank funding margins and green bond coupons

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual result: net property income $120.8m (+3.3%), NPAT $127.7m, net distributable income $60.9m (+9.1%), NTA per share $1.60 (up from $1.53), gearing 37.2% (36.1% post-settlement), full-year dividend 6.65 cps in line with guidance
Dividend policy changed from AFFO-based to FFO-based, targeting 80-95% payout of FFO to reduce year-to-year volatility; DRP suspended for Q4 dividend following divestment proceeds
FY2027 dividend guidance retained at 6.65 cps despite 'increased market uncertainty'
143 Lambton Quay, Wellington settled for $6 million
4 Henderson Place, Auckland settled for $40 million; proceeds applied to debt reduction
ARG010 green bonds ($100m) matured and were repaid; syndicated bank facilities refinanced/upsized to $725m across five banks with new 7-year Tranche C (to July 2032) and Tranche E added
224 Neilson Street Warehouse A reached practical completion (11,475sqm, 6 Green Star Design and Built); Warehouse B fully leased to Basick Transport

NZ Government outlined proposed earthquake-prone building regime reform, replacing the NBS framework and largely excluding low-seismic Auckland; viewed by Argosy management as a positive sector development
Practical completion of Mt Richmond Stage 1 Warehouse 6 (5,833sqm), leased to global pharmaceutical distributor Viatris Limited

Key Wellington government tenant retentions: NZ Post renewed at 7WQ (6-year renewal to Dec-2031); MBIE extended at 15 Stout St for a further 9 years from July 2026, including a $13m decarbonisation retrofit project
CEO Peter Mence to step down by the 2027 AGM with succession search underway; Chair Jeff Morrison to be succeeded by Martin Stearne following the 2027 AGM

items.notes: Consistent with FY2026 actual; retained despite management flagging 'increased market uncertainty'; sits within new FFO payout policy of 80-95%
Replaces prior AFFO-based policy; intended to reduce dividend volatility caused by maintenance capex, leasing incentive and swap close-out cost swings
Currently 55%; to be achieved via green development pipeline (Mt Richmond, Neilson Street) and non-core divestments

items.target: 50% of portfolio by value certified green
items.notes: Currently 39% (including Warehouse 6 at Mt Richmond); tied to a 17.5% emissions reduction target by FY31
37.2% at FY2026 year-end, falling to 36.1% following settlement of held-for-sale properties; bank covenant ceiling is 50%

items.target: Six identified properties, combined book value $139 million
items.notes: Follows FY2026 sales of 4 Henderson Place ($40m) and 143 Lambton Quay ($6m); proceeds earmarked initially for debt reduction

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Jeff Morrison: 'Argosy is well positioned, supported by a strong balance sheet and a growing, high-quality and diversified portfolio with a clear focus on sustainability and green assets.' Management flagged that leasing enquiry has improved recently but may be affected by broader market uncertainty tied to geopolitical tensions; the team remains focused on addressing vacancy and near-term lease expiries while maintaining tenant retention. FY27 guidance was explicitly retained rather than raised 'as a result of increased market uncertainty.'

bull_case: Embedded rent reversion — portfolio is 9.3% under-rented ex-development market rent, providing multi-year mark-to-market upside as leases renew, evidenced by 3.5% annualised rental growth on FY2026 reviews

Falling interest rate cycle (OCR at 2.25%, weighted average debt cost down to 4.65% from 5.11%) directly boosts distributable income and supports further cap-rate compression/valuation gains after two consecutive years of revaluation gains

Green industrial development pipeline (224 Neilson Street, Mt Richmond) is fully/near-fully pre-leased and shifts the portfolio mix toward the structurally favoured, better-fundamentals industrial sector

Potential earthquake-prone building regulatory reform would meaningfully cut compliance/remediation cost overhang across the NZ property sector, disproportionately benefiting Auckland-weighted owners like Argosy

Conservative, in-target-band gearing (37.2%, trending to 36.1%) and diversified $725m five-bank funding plus green bonds provide balance sheet flexibility to fund the development pipeline without forced equity issuance
bear_case: Sub-scale diversified strategy lacks the sector leadership of pure-play peers (Goodman in industrial, Precinct in premium office), potentially capping structural re-rating versus specialists

Wellington office and government tenant exposure (~25% of value, ~31% of rental income) remains vulnerable to public sector fiscal restraint and further government space consolidation despite recent key lease renewals

Reported profit and NTA are heavily reliant on favourable independent revaluations ($58.5m FY2026, $72.7m FY2025); a reversal in cap-rate sentiment or bond yields would quickly erode NTA and distort headline earnings

Dividend held flat at 6.65 cps for FY2027 amid explicit management caution on 'increased market uncertainty,' with a newly adopted FFO payout policy signalling underlying distributable cash flow volatility

Extended leasing decision timeframes and softer enquiry noted through FY2026 suggest tenant demand recovery is not yet assured, and occupancy (94.6%) plus a sizeable multi-year lease expiry profile leave execution risk in re-leasing vacant/expiring space
